il6_registered_instrument.exposure: soluble interleukin-6 receptor (sIL-6R) blood levels, exposure coefficients from the van Dongen 2014 GWAS
il6_registered_instrument.instruments: IL6R-region cis instruments on chromosome 1: rs2228145 as the single-SNP instrument (rs4129267 and rs12126142 as r2 > 0.99 proxies where rs2228145 is unavailable); the primary PCA-IVW analysis uses 491 SNPs reduced to 4 principal components
il6_registered_instrument.outcome_definition: UK Biobank 'recurrent depressive symptoms', defined from self-reported symptoms (analytic sample n = 89,119); the paper replicates in PGC MDD 2018 clinical MDD, OR 1.016 (1.003-1.029)
il6_registered_instrument.n_cases_note: The UK Biobank case count for the primary outcome is given only in the supplemental note, which is not served by PMC; the analytic sample is n = 89,119. The PGC MDD 2018 replication sample has 59,851 cases and 113,514 controls.
il6_registered_instrument.direction_note: The estimate is per 10^-8 g/mL increase in sIL-6R, and OR > 1 means higher sIL-6R raises the odds of depression. Higher sIL-6R is the rs2228145 minor-allele direction, which reduces IL-6 classical signaling, so OR > 1 is the direction indexing reduced classical IL6R signaling. The registered rule is sign-blind, so direction does not enter the classification.
il6_registered_instrument.source_sentence: Results are consistent with a causal effect of sIL-6R on depression (PCA-IVW Odds Ratio: 1.023 (95% Confidence Interval: 1.006-1.039), p = 0.006).
il6_registered_instrument.source_location: Abstract, Results; restated in the Results section ('a 10-8 g/mL increase in sIL-6R was associated with 1.023 times higher odds of depression (95% Confidence Interval: 1.006 - 1.039, p=0.006)') and in Table 2, UK Biobank column, PCA-IVW row: 1.023 (1.006-1.039), 0.006, 491 (4 PCs)
il6_registered_instrument.query: IL6R AND "mendelian randomization" AND (depression OR "major depressive disorder")
